findings.summary: Cargo stops at the first failing test binary, so the parsed list misses tests that never ran, and the per-test rule can still excuse new failures
findings.evidence: athena.toml configures the test check as `run = ["cargo", "test", "--locked"]` (lines 96 and 122). A grep for `no-fail-fast` over crates/ finds nothing. By default, cargo test stops after the first test binary that fails. Suppose the base fails test X in binary A. The candidate also fails X in A, and it breaks Y in binary B, which runs after A. The candidate's output then lists only {X}. Under the plan, {X} is a subset of the base's {X}, so the check is marked pre-existing, the verdict passes, and Y never ran. The plan also expects lists from several binaries in one run (Decision 3, Risk 3), but the configured command does not produce them. This is the same 'unjudged' gap the failure class is about. Fix: Have the comparison know whether the test run was complete. One option: run_check adds `--no-fail-fast` to test-kind checks whose command is `cargo test`. This lives in code, not in athena.toml, so the out-of-scope rule on governance files is kept. Another option: parse the binaries that ran (the `Running`/`Doc-tests` lines) and cargo's stop marker (`error: test failed, to rerun pass ...` without a 'targets failed' summary). Treat a stopped run as incomplete and fall back to calling it new, or report that the remaining tests did not run, instead of excusing it. Add a verify.rs or checks.rs test for the case where both runs stop early at the same binary.
findings.location: Approach / Decision 2 (per-test is_pre_existing) and Decision 3 (qualify by binary); athena.toml:96,122

findings.summary: Failing test names go into records without passing through the redactor
findings.evidence: `output_tail` is stored as `ctx.redactor.redact(&tail(&output, TAIL_BYTES))?`. The plan fills `failed_tests` from the full raw output 'before the tail is cut' and says nothing about redaction. The new field is then written into Baseline and verdict records. Fix: Pass each parsed name through `ctx.redactor.redact` (or redact the full output once before parsing) so the new field gets the same handling as output_tail.
findings.location: Step 2 / checks.rs run_check (output_tail redacted at line 276)

findings.summary: The producer cannot read the two jobs' quoted output, so 'real shapes' needs a concrete source
findings.evidence: System facts: the producer snapshot has no `records/` and no history, so the output recorded in jobs 20261017-044408-wcwy and 20261017-182453-a5sf cannot be read there. Criterion 3 asks for the shapes quoted in those jobs. Fix: Say where the fixtures come from. For example, embed literal text in cargo's exact format (`Running unittests src/lib.rs (target/debug/deps/<crate>-<hash>)`, a `failures:` stdout block, then the indented `failures:` list and `test result: FAILED`), copied from a real local run with one deliberately failing test. Include a doc-test case and a run where cargo stopped early.
findings.location: Demonstration for criterion 3; Risk 3 ('Test on real output shapes quoted in the two jobs')

findings.summary: Choose the finding's severity now rather than leaving it to the producer
findings.evidence: judge already pushes `check {} failed` for blocking checks (verify.rs:302–304), so the verdict already fails. The plan leaves Major versus Minor to whatever happens when send_back tests run. Fix: Decide the severity in the plan. Minor (informational) avoids counting the same failure twice. Add a send_back test that pins how it is counted.
findings.location: Decision 4 / Open question on finding severity

summary: The plan reads the request correctly and puts the fix in the right place. Pre-existing detection is decided by name only, in `Baseline::failed_before` (records.rs:2490), which `verify::is_pre_existing` calls (verify.rs:134–136). `run_check` (checks.rs:190) builds both the baseline runs and the candidate runs (`baseline_runs`, checks.rs:286), so one new field on `CheckRun` covers both sides. Every function and test helper the plan names exists: `judge`, `mark_pre_existing`, `held_for_timeout`, `athena_finding`, `baseline_with`, `judge_against` and `sh_spec`. Each demonstration uses real production entry points, no doubles, and would fail without the change. Athena's eight minor scope findings are covered by the plan's own reason: Rust will not compile a struct literal that leaves out a field. I agree with that reason and do not repeat them. One soundness problem blocks acceptance. The configured test check is `cargo test --locked` (athena.toml lines 96 and 122), and nothing in the crates passes `--no-fail-fast`. Cargo stops at the first test binary that fails, so the parsed failure list only covers the tests that actually ran. If the base and the candidate both stop at the same failing binary with {X}, the plan marks the failure pre-existing and the job passes, even though binaries the job broke never ran. The plan claims a check is excused only when "every failing test also failed on the base", but in the configured setup it cannot know that. The fault this job is meant to remove stays open. The planner can fix this, so the verdict is revise.
